terms.gloss: part; in phrases, a respect: omnī ex parte, in every respect
evidence: Cic. Lael. 79: quod sit omnī ex parte in suō genere perfectum
Cic. Att. 7.3.3: ex parte magnā tibi adsentior
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: omnī (ex, ā) parte, “in every respect, entirely”; ex magnā parte, in great part; in omnēs partēs, in every respect (Cic. Att. 11.6.2).

terms.grammar: phrase: attinet with ad and the accusative
evidence: Cic. Att. 16.14.4: hominem, quod ad mē attinet, nōn ingrātum
Plancus in Cic. Fam. 10.9.2: quod ad mē attinet, mī Cicerō

phrases.latin: nec quicquam difficilius quam reperīre quod sit omnī ex parte in suō genere perfectum
phrases.english: and nothing is harder than to find something perfect of its kind in every respect

phrases.latin: habet enim rēs dēlīberātiōnem; etsī ex parte magnā tibi adsentior
phrases.english: for the matter needs thinking over, though in many respects I agree with you

phrases.latin: Brundisī jacēre in omnīs partīs est molestum.
phrases.english: Lying idle at Brundisium is irksome in every respect.

sources: Lewis & Short: pars · Lewis & Short: attineo
